subject: Notice: proposed subprocessor (AnalyticsCo) and evidence deliverables
messages:
From: Emma Dunn <emma.dunn@cloudshift.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed addition of AnalyticsCo as subprocessor / Order Form attached

Hi Jonas / Laura / Kim,

Quick heads-up: CloudShift is planning to route a subset of telemetry enrichment to a new analytics vendor, AnalyticsCo (Tariq Shah, cc'd). They will only process hashed identifiers and aggregated metrics per the SOW. We're attaching the updated Order Form and the vendor's proposed DPA for your review.

Attachments: OrderForm_CloudShift_v3.pdf (pdf), DPA_AnalyticsCo_proposed.docx (docx)

High-level:
- Scope: event enrichment + retention 30 days (transient KV cache)
- Data type: pseudonymized identifiers, aggregated metrics
- Location: us-east-1

Can Redwood confirm whether the proposed flow-down meets our DPA flow-down requirements and whether any additional redlines are required (encryption at rest, KMS, subprocessor notification cadence)?

Target timeline: CloudShift is hoping to sign the order form by 5/24 to meet their release. If we need additional evidence (SOC2 snapshot, architecture diagram), they can provide it by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Emma Dunn
Procurement Manager | CloudShift Inc.
emma.dunn@cloudshift.com

Laura / Kim — thanks for the heads-up, Emma. Quick internal plan:

1) Laura (Legal): please triage the DPA redlines and highlight any non-starter clauses. Priorities: flow-down of data processing limitations, deletion paths, and audit rights.
2) Kim (Procurement): confirm whether the Order Form terms and billing cadence match our commercial commitments to CloudShift (they have a partial commitment under CF-4821). Also please confirm whether we require AnalyticsCo to be on our approved vendor list or if an exception is acceptable.
3) I'll respond to CloudShift with a conditional approval timeline once we have legal sign-off and evidence.

If useful, let's do a quick 15-min sync at 10:30 PT.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Proposed addition of AnalyticsCo as subprocessor / Order Form attached

Thanks, Jonas. I reviewed the vendor DPA and pulled a short redline summary (attached). Top issues:

- Encryption / KMS: proposed DPA leaves encryption controls at vendor discretion; we need explicit AES-256 at rest + customer KMS keywrap or justification for not supporting KMS.
- Subprocessor notice: vendor proposes 30 days notice; we prefer 14 days and prior written consent for changes that increase access to unredacted PII.
- Audit rights: vendor limits audits to quarterly self-attestations. We need right-to-audit for Redwood and a SOC2 Type II report (or equivalent) on demand.
- Deletion / export: contract language lacks a clear data return/deletion procedure aligned with our retention expectations.

Recommended path: produce a DPA_redlines_Legal_20270518.docx with tracked changes and request the following evidence in the next 48 hours: SOC2 snapshot, network diagram showing separation, and encryption key management paper. If they can provide those items, we can likely accept AnalyticsCo with the redlines.

Attachment: DPA_redlines_Legal_20270518.docx

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Emma Dunn <emma.dunn@cloudshift.com>, Tariq Shah <tariq.shah@analyticsco.io>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Proposed addition of AnalyticsCo as subprocessor / Order Form attached

Emma / Tariq — thanks for sending. Per our internal review (cc'd Laura and Kim), Redwood can provisionally accept AnalyticsCo as a subprocessor subject to the following gating items:

1) Execution of the attached redlined DPA (we've returned tracked changes).
2) Delivery of evidence: SOC2 Type II snapshot (or equivalent), architecture diagram showing tenant separation, and confirmation of KMS usage or justification.
3) Order Form: please sign the updated OrderForm_CloudShift_v3.pdf and route via DocuSign. Link below.

Mutual action plan / timeline (requested by CloudShift):
- 5/19 EOD: AnalyticsCo to provide SOC2 snapshot + architecture diagram + KMS statement
- 5/20 AM: Redwood Legal to confirm DPA redlines are acceptable or provide final changes
- 5/20 EOD: DocuSign signature on Order Form

DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/recipient?envelopeId=12345-CloudShift-OF

If the vendor can meet the evidence timeline, we'll proceed to execution and add AnalyticsCo to our approved vendor list for this account. If anything slips, we will require a temporary hold (no production ingestion) until approvals are complete.

Thanks,
Jonas
From: Tariq Shah <tariq.shah@analyticsco.io>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, emma.dunn@cloudshift.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Proposed addition of AnalyticsCo as subprocessor / Order Form attached

Hi Jonas / Emma / team — thanks for the clear plan. Per the timetable, attaching the SOC2 snapshot and a short architecture diagram. Please find: analyticsco-soc2-snapshot.pdf (SOC2 snapshot) and a one-page design diagram embedded in the doc.

Short notes:
- AnalyticsCo uses AES-256 encryption at rest and supports customer-managed keys via AWS KMS (we can enable a keywrap flow; confirm the AWS account ID and we will set the policy).
- We can accept the 14-day prior-notice for subprocessor changes and are happy to agree to the right-to-audit language in redline.

We will counter-sign the DocuSign envelope once Redwood confirms the redlines are acceptable.

Best,
Tariq Shah
VP Product | AnalyticsCo
Tariq.Shah@analyticsco.io

Attachments: analyticsco-soc2-snapshot.pdf
